title: Unit test record
body:
Unit test record is one entry in the Generated Code and Program Test Corpus Database. It describes a practical, reusable unit of work: what the entry covers, how it is applied, and how its result is checked before it is trusted. The entry is written in plain sentences so a reader can follow it without specialist tooling, and every claim in it is tied to a check that can be repeated.

In practice, the unit test record works by first naming its inputs clearly, then applying a defined method step by step, and finally recording the outcome together with the evidence that supports it. Inputs are listed before work begins, so missing or ambiguous inputs are caught early rather than discovered after the result is produced. Each step leaves a trace, which means a later reviewer can retrace the work from its inputs to its conclusion without guessing.

Quality control for the unit test record rests on four checks. The schema check confirms every required field is present and well formed. The completeness check confirms the entry covers its stated scope and does not silently omit a part. The consistency check confirms the entry agrees with the other entries in this database and does not contradict them. The demo check confirms the accompanying program actually runs and produces the recorded output, so the entry is demonstrated rather than merely asserted.

The unit test record is useful wherever the same kind of work repeats. A team can reuse the entry instead of redesigning the approach each time, and can compare results across uses because the method and the checks stay the same. Limits are stated honestly: where a result depends on judgment, on data quality, or on conditions outside the entry, the entry says so, and it does not claim a live deployment or an outcome that has not been measured.
